classification.difficultyReason: Express all individual times relative to the unknown joint time and reframe those times as additive reciprocal work rates before solving and interpreting the resulting quadratic.

content.prompt: A, B and C do a piece of work together. A could have done it alone in six hours longer, B in 15 hours longer and C in twice the time. How long did it take all three to do the work together?

answer.short:
$3\text{ hours}$

Add the individual fractions of the job completed per hour.
answer.worked:
Let $t$ hours be their time working together, with $t>0$. Alone, A, B and C take $t+6$, $t+15$ and $2t$ hours respectively. Their rates add to the joint rate.
$$\begin{align*}\frac1{t+6}+\frac1{t+15}+\frac1{2t}&=\frac1t\\2t(t+15)+2t(t+6)+(t+6)(t+15)&=2(t+6)(t+15)\\4t^2+42t&=t^2+21t+90\\3t^2+21t-90&=0\\t^2+7t-30&=0\\(t+10)(t-3)&=0\\t&=-10\text{ or }3\end{align*}$$
Reject the negative time. Together they took $3$ hours. Check: their individual times are $9$, $18$ and $6$ hours, and $\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{18}+\frac{1}{6}=\frac{1}{3}$ of the job per hour.
